text:
**Yes. If Monzo Bank fails, the UK’s Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) protects up to £120,000 per person in eligible cash deposits held with Monzo.** Monzo is a licensed UK bank, so its customers get the same deposit protection as customers of a UK high-street bank. In most cases, the FSCS pays you back automatically within seven working days; you don’t need to make a claim. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/faq?utm_source=openai))

The key is that the limit is **per person, not per account**. Add together your Monzo current account, regular Pots, savings held by Monzo itself and your share of any joint account. If that total is £120,000 or less, your eligible cash is fully covered. Two joint holders can have up to £240,000 covered between them, provided neither exceeds their individual limit. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/budgeting-overdrafts-savings/instant-access-savings-pots-web?utm_source=openai))

If you keep **more than £120,000** at Monzo long term, you can protect the excess by moving it to a bank with a separate banking licence. For a temporary balance from a qualifying event, such as selling your main home, the FSCS can cover up to £1.4 million for six months. ([protected.fscs.org.uk](https://protected.fscs.org.uk/check/check-your-money-is-protected/?utm_source=openai))
